hook.line: When you describe how things usually are, an essay or a boss will pounce on one exception. Spanish has a few small phrases that make a generalisation safe, and honest.
hook.es: Por lo general, los clientes llegan temprano.

examples.es: Por lo general, los clientes llegan temprano.
Por regla general, no aceptamos devoluciones.
examples.en: As a rule, we don't accept returns.

examples.es: En general, la gente fue muy amable.
examples.en: On the whole, people were very kind.

examples.es: Hernando pide un tinto, salvo excepciones.
examples.en: Hernando orders a black coffee, with some exceptions.

examples.es: Por lo general, los barrios cambian despacio.
¿Qué hace usted por lo general los domingos?
examples.en: What do you usually do on Sundays? (formal)

rule:
These phrases say "this is true most of the time" and leave the door open for exceptions.

*Por lo general*, *por regla general* and *en general* all start a sentence, followed by a comma, or sit after the verb.

*Salvo excepciones* means "with some exceptions". Add it at the end to show you know the rule has gaps.

It is not *siempre* (always) or *nunca* (never). Those claim there are no exceptions. English "generally" is the nearest word, but Spanish likes the longer phrase, especially in writing.
smallPrint: Teachers call these *adverbial phrases of generalisation*. They hedge a claim rather than state it flatly.

readAndPick.es: Por lo general, Hernando pide un tinto.
options: Generally, Hernando orders a black coffee.
Hernando always orders a black coffee.
Hernando is ordering a black coffee now.

readAndPick.es: Los clientes pagan en efectivo, salvo excepciones.
options: The customers never pay in cash.
The customers pay in cash, with some exceptions.
The customers pay in cash, without exception.

readAndPick.es: Por regla general, no aceptamos devoluciones.
options: We didn't accept returns.
We never accept returns.
As a rule, we don't accept returns.

readAndPick.es: En general, la gente fue muy amable.
options: On the whole, people were very kind.
A few people were very kind.
Everybody was very kind.
Generally, everyone arrives late.
Everyone arrives late, without exception.
Almost everyone arrives late.

readAndPick.es: ¿Qué hace usted por lo general los domingos?
options: What did you do last Sunday? (formal)
What are you doing this Sunday? (formal)
What do you usually do on Sundays? (formal)

readAndPick.es: Salvo excepciones, el café abre a las siete.
options: With few exceptions, the café opens at seven.
The café always opens at seven.
The café never opens at seven.

readAndPick.es: Por lo general, no salgo de noche.
options: I never go out at night.
Generally, I don't go out at night.
I didn't go out last night.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *Por lo general* or *Siempre* and type the whole sentence, admitting that exceptions exist: *___, los clientes llegan temprano, salvo excepciones.*
yourTurn.answer: Por lo general, los clientes llegan temprano, salvo excepciones.
yourTurn.why: *Siempre* claims there are no exceptions, so it clashes with *salvo excepciones*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Generally, neighbourhoods change slowly.
yourTurn.answer: Por lo general, los barrios cambian despacio.
accept: Los barrios cambian despacio por lo general.
En general, los barrios cambian despacio.
yourTurn.why: *Por lo general* opens the sentence and is followed by a comma.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: As a rule, we don't accept returns.
yourTurn.answer: Por regla general, no aceptamos devoluciones.
accept: No aceptamos devoluciones por regla general.
yourTurn.why: *Por regla general* says it is the rule, and *no* goes with the verb as usual.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: On the whole, people were very kind.
yourTurn.answer: En general, la gente fue muy amable.
accept: La gente fue muy amable en general.
yourTurn.why: *En general* is the short, everyday way to say "on the whole".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it hedged: *Hernando pide un tinto.* Say: Hernando orders a black coffee, with some exceptions.
yourTurn.answer: Hernando pide un tinto, salvo excepciones.
accept: Salvo excepciones, Hernando pide un tinto.
yourTurn.why: *Salvo excepciones* closes the sentence and admits the rule has gaps.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, asking someone formally: What do you usually do on Sundays?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Qué hace usted por lo general los domingos?
accept: ¿Qué hace por lo general los domingos?
Por lo general, ¿qué hace usted los domingos?
yourTurn.why: *Por lo general* can sit inside a question too, and *hace* is the *usted* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Generally, I don't go out at night.
yourTurn.answer: Por lo general, no salgo de noche.
accept: No salgo de noche por lo general.
En general, no salgo de noche.
yourTurn.why: The phrase stands outside the sentence, so *no* stays in front of the verb.

pitfalls.wrong: Por lo generales, los clientes llegan temprano.
pitfalls.right: Por lo general, los clientes llegan temprano.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The phrase is fixed: *general* never changes to a plural.

pitfalls.wrong: Por general, los clientes llegan temprano.
pitfalls.right: Por lo general, los clientes llegan temprano.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You need *lo* in the middle: *por lo general*.

pitfalls.right: Por lo general, llegan temprano, salvo excepciones.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Siempre* means no exceptions, so it fights with *salvo excepciones*.

personal: Say something that is generally true about your week or your city, then add *salvo excepciones*.
